newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean ruling party leader wants dialogue.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean ruling party leader wants dialogue.

text.p: South Korea's ruling party chairman on Thursday said he still wanted dialogue to avert a crisis over a controversial labour law and promised steps to allay worker fears it could lead to layoffs.
The remarks by Lee Hong-koo came a day after state prosecutors issued an ultimatum to strike leaders to drop industrial action immediately or face arrest.
"I would like to use this occasion to make it known again my willingness to resolve all problems through dialogue and compromise," Lee told a news conference.
Lee's New Korea Party rammed through parliament the labour bill at a brief dawn session in the absence of opposition deputies on December 26, sparking three weeks of wildcat strikes.
"If there are disadvantages caused by this labour legislation, I and the New Korea Party will lead efforts to minimise them," he said.
"We will do our utmost to prepare various follow-up steps to end fears of employment and the problem of unemployment," he added.
